title: Initialize repo history and enable bd sync
description: Git repo exists but has no commits and everything is untracked. Make an initial commit, then run bd sync so beads are persisted in git (per AGENTS.md workflow).

close_reason: Created initial git commit and ran bd sync successfully; issues.jsonl is tracked.

title: ROI/parcel anchor projectors for anatomy-guided functional alignment
description: Add primitives to build per-subject anchor projectors (anchors x native) from ROI/parcellation definitions (hard or soft weights), and a guided alignment path that uses these projectors to condition functional alignment (not anatomy-only). Must support differing native dimensions across subjects.
close_reason: Added ROI anchor projectors (roi_anchor_projector/s) and set_roi_guidance() guidance channels

title: Fix legacy beads database fingerprint
description: bd commands emit 'LEGACY DATABASE DETECTED' warning because .beads/beads.db lacks repository fingerprint (pre-0.17.5). Run 'bd migrate --update-repo-id' (or re-init .beads if appropriate) so bd daemon/sync can work reliably and avoid accidental DB reuse across repos.
acceptance_criteria: bd commands run without legacy DB warning; bd daemon can start; bd sync works once repo has commits.
close_reason: Ran bd migrate --update-repo-id; legacy DB warning resolved and daemon runs.

title: Wire observation-axis CV into fit_alignment()
description:
NOTE: This is now tracked under epic neuralign-8d7 (observation-axis crossfit orchestration).

Preferred implementation: add run_obs_crossfit_alignment() (fold-wise train/test runner) + run_obs_crossfit_from_data() (slicing wrapper) and then, optionally, have fit_alignment() branch on cv_folds=='observation' and delegate to the wrapper.

Original intent preserved:
- Accept create_obs_folds() output (axis='observation')
- Fit transforms on train observations only
- Apply to held-out observations
- Enforce anchor semantics (common anchor vs fold-specific)

Dependency: blocked on neuralign-8d7.3.
close_reason: Implemented and tested

title: Intrinsic geometry coordinates (Laplacian eigenmodes) as anatomical guidance
description: Add support for computing template-free intrinsic geometry coordinates per subject (e.g., Laplacian eigenmodes / diffusion maps) from surface/voxel adjacency graphs, and define how they guide functional alignment (e.g., as extra features/regularizers or costs for OT). Must support differing native dimensions.
close_reason: Added Laplacian eigenmode guidance (laplacian_eigenmodes) and set_intrinsic_geometry_guidance()

title: Observation-axis folds: run/blocked_time
description: Add create_obs_folds() for run-based and blocked-time folds, supporting per-subject obs id vectors and avoiding brittle global intersections.
close_reason: Added create_obs_folds() for run and blocked_time strategies with intersection/union id policies

title: Export shared alignment primitives for fmrireg.*
description: Add exported primitives in neuralign (Procrustes rotation/distance with explicit convention + scaling, Procrustes-based reference selection, observation-axis fold construction, and feature-block stacking/harmonization) so fmrireg.gnef/garrr/lowrank can delegate instead of reimplementing.
close_reason: Exported shared Procrustes, reference distance, obs-folds, and feature-block helpers; added tests + docs

title: Fix compose_alignment() provenance loss
description:
compose_alignment() builds a detailed provenance object at compose.R:115-129 containing composed_from, composed_at, and neuralign_version, but this provenance is NEVER passed to the AlignmentModel constructor.

The AlignmentModel() constructor (alignment_model.R:58-107) has no provenance parameter and always builds its own generic provenance. The composed model ends up with params=list() and no record of the source models.

Fix options:
1. Add provenance parameter to AlignmentModel() constructor
2. Pass composed provenance through params and merge in constructor
3. Use new('AlignmentModel', ...) directly to set provenance slot

Composition is a core story for structural→functional pipelines; provenance here is important for reproducibility.
close_reason: Implemented and tested

title: Support sparse-label overlap via Procrustes graph synchronization
description: Implement a graph-based Procrustes alignment method for subjects with partially overlapping obs_labels (possibly empty global intersection) but a connected overlap graph. Compute pairwise Procrustes on overlaps (using procrustes_rotation), then solve for globally consistent transforms via orthogonal synchronization/rotation averaging. Provide diagnostics for disconnected graphs and minimum overlap thresholds.
close_reason: Implemented procrustes_graph aligner (graph-synchronized Procrustes on sparse label overlap) with registration + tests

title: Add obs_labels to AlignmentData and validate shared observation labels
description: Add an obs_labels field to AlignmentData plus validation that (when provided) enforces a shared observation label system across subjects (length matches n_obs, labels non-NA, optional colnames consistency). Thread through as_alignment_data()/validate_alignment_data() and ensure fit_alignment checks labels when present.
close_reason: Implemented AlignmentData@obs_labels, get_obs_labels(), label validation, and threading via fit_alignment/run_cv_alignment. Added tests and docs.

title: Make package skeleton pass R CMD check
description: Current repo has DESCRIPTION Collate entries and code references (e.g., AlignmentModel() calls get_aligner()) for files/functions that are missing. Add minimal stubs/implementations (AlignmentResult, registry, fit/apply, etc.) or prune DESCRIPTION/exports so the package builds cleanly.
acceptance_criteria: R CMD check runs without missing-file/missing-symbol errors.
close_reason: completed

title: Procrustes primitives: scaling + convention-safe helpers
description: Fix .procrustes_single(scale=TRUE) and export convention-safe helpers (procrustes_rotation/procrustes_distance) so downstream packages can reuse a single implementation.
close_reason: Implemented exported Procrustes rotation/distance helpers with scaling + label-overlap support

title: Observation-axis crossfit orchestration
description:
Add a first-class observation-axis crossfit runner (fold-wise train/test over observations, not subjects) so downstream packages (fmrireg.lowrank / fmrireg.gnef / dkge) stop re-implementing fold bookkeeping, leakage guards, and anchor/reference semantics.

Scope:
- Export run_obs_crossfit_alignment() that consumes fold-wise train/test matrices (features × obs) and optional fold-wise obs_labels.
- Standard return object (ObsCrossfitAlignment) with models/transforms/aligned_test_by_fold + provenance + warnings.
- Explicit anchor semantics via anchor_policy to prevent invalid aggregation when references are fold-specific.
- Optional wrapper that slices an AlignmentData using create_obs_folds() indices.

title: Implement ObsCrossfitAlignment + run_obs_crossfit_alignment()
description:
Implement run_obs_crossfit_alignment(train_data_by_fold, test_data_by_fold, obs_labels_train/test, method, reference, anchor_policy, ...) that:
- Fits per-fold AlignmentModel on train matrices only.
- Applies fold transforms to test matrices (if provided).
- Normalizes/validates obs_labels inputs (vector vs per-subject list vs per-fold) and enforces length == ncol.
- Returns a standard ObsCrossfitAlignment object:
  - models_by_fold, transforms_by_fold, aligned_test_by_fold (optional), fold_info, anchor_common, reference_kind, provenance, warnings.

Acceptance:
- Unit tests cover: train-only fitting, test-only application, obs_labels normalization cases, method+reference passthrough.

title: Anchor policy + template mapping for obs crossfit
description:
Add explicit anchor/reference semantics to run_obs_crossfit_alignment():

- Detect reference_kind per fold: template | fixed_subject | data_driven.
- Determine anchor_common across folds.
- Enforce anchor_policy:
  - common_or_error: error unless fixed subject or explicit template.
  - fold_specific_ok: allow but set anchor_common=FALSE and attach warnings.
  - map_to_template: require template + template_obs_labels; map fold-wise results to that template anchor.

Acceptance:
- Tests: data-driven reference triggers error under common_or_error; allowed under fold_specific_ok; template mapping requires template and results marked anchor_common=TRUE.

title: Wrapper: run_obs_crossfit_from_data(data, obs_folds)
description:
Add a convenience wrapper for timepoint-axis crossfit:

run_obs_crossfit_from_data(data, obs_folds, method, reference, anchor_policy, ...) where obs_folds is output from create_obs_folds(). The wrapper:
- Slices per-subject columns into train/test matrices by fold.
- Calls run_obs_crossfit_alignment() under the hood.
- Stores fold provenance (guard_tr, fold ids, id_policy, common_ids).

Acceptance:
- Tests: correct slicing for run-based folds; correct behavior when subjects have differing run id sets.

title: Docs: observation-axis crossfit + anchor semantics
description:
Documentation updates:
- Add a short vignette section explaining observation-axis crossfit vs subject-CV.
- Explain anchor_common / reference_kind / anchor_policy and how to aggregate fold outputs safely.
- Include minimal runnable examples for design-labeled patterns (K×P) and timepoint folds (run-based).

Acceptance:
- Vignette renders; examples run under R CMD check.

title: fit_alignment obs-CV: resolve reference per fold + optional fold transforms
description:
Improve the existing fit_alignment(..., cv_folds=<obs folds>) code path (.fit_cv_obs_folds):

- Resolve reference within each fold using only train observations (and only training subjects if applicable), so reference="medoid"/"consensus" works consistently across aligners.
- Record anchor semantics correctly:
  - set anchor_common based on reference_kind (fixed_subject/template vs data-driven),
  - store anchor_by_fold and/or warnings when anchors are fold-specific.
- Add an option to retain fold-specific transforms in cv_info (e.g., transforms_by_fold[[fold]][[subject]]) to support downstream fold-wise statistics rotation without reimplementing CV loops.

Acceptance:
- Tests cover: reference resolution in obs-CV folds; anchor_common flag correctness; fold transform retention when enabled.

title: Handle topofmri non-exported helpers
description: topofmri helpers like graph_from_neurovec()/align_to_template() exist but are not exported. Ensure neuralign integrations use exported topofmri entry points (align_epifmri/fit_topo_template) or coordinate upstream exports; avoid topofmri::: usage in core.
acceptance_criteria: No reliance on non-exported topofmri symbols in neuralign core; integration tests use exported API.

title: Embedding methods: apply_alignment/compose_alignment guardrails
description: Make apply_alignment() and compose_alignment() check method capabilities and either (a) handle embedding-returning methods via their apply_fn/operator output, or (b) error early with guidance. Avoid silent misuse of operator-only code paths.
acceptance_criteria: apply_alignment()/compose_alignment() refuse unsupported embedding modes with clear messages; supported embedding providers work via declared operators.
close_reason: Added operator-only guardrails: apply_alignment now uses apply_transform (with matrix/operator checks) and compose_alignment/check_composition validate matrix transforms; added transform validation in fit_alignment CV paths.

title: Support sparse-label + anatomy-guided functional alignment (3 methods)
description: Roadmap/umbrella for: (1) sparse-label overlap graph alignment (Procrustes synchronization), (2) ROI/parcel anchor projectors for anatomy-guided alignment with variable native dims, and (3) intrinsic geometry guidance (Laplacian eigenmodes) for resting-state embeddings. Includes docs/vignette.
close_reason: All three methods implemented (procrustes_graph, ROI projector guidance, intrinsic geometry guidance) plus vignette

title: Embedding methods: enforce contract at registration
description: If an aligner advertises capabilities='embedding', validate required fields (at minimum: must provide transforms operators or a custom apply_fn that yields operators). Add early, actionable error messages.
acceptance_criteria: register_aligner(returns='embedding') errors early unless required hooks are present; error message tells provider how to comply.
close_reason: register_aligner() now validates capabilities and rejects returns='embedding' with actionable guidance; added test coverage.

description: Extend select_reference() to support distance='procrustes' (with label intersection support) for medoid/centroid selection.
close_reason: Added distance='procrustes' to select_reference with overlap-aware pairwise distances

title: Use .is_matrixish() for template reference detection everywhere
description:
Currently ~12 locations use is.matrix() to detect template references, but .is_matrixish() (which also handles sparse Matrix objects) exists in validate_transforms.R:9-11 and is not used in reference handling. This means sparse Matrix templates silently fail.

Files to fix:
- R/fit_alignment.R (.resolve_reference, .reference_kind)
- R/reference.R (.validate_reference_for_method, get_reference_data)
- R/alignment_model.R (show method)
- R/aligner_procrustes.R (template detection in fit functions)
- R/aligner_ot.R (template detection)
- R/cv.R (reference_kind inline check)
- R/serialize.R (export template detection)

Also add 'template' to .procrustes_capabilities$reference_types (currently only 'subject','consensus').
close_reason: Implemented and tested

title: Docs/vignette: choosing alignment anchors for sparse labels vs resting state
description: Write a short vignette describing when to use (a) shared labels, (b) overlap-graph synchronization, (c) shared feature spaces, (d) ROI anchors, and (e) intrinsic geometry guidance; include minimal runnable examples using neuralign primitives.
close_reason: Added anchors vignette (vignettes/anchors.Rmd) covering sparse labels, ROI anchors, and intrinsic geometry guidance

title: Define CV axes and fold-safe reference selection
description: Specify and implement what cv indices refer to (subject-level vs within-subject observation/run/task). Ensure reference selection occurs within each training fold for subject-level CV, and define cross-fitting hooks for within-subject leakage control (e.g., gnef Mode B patterns).
acceptance_criteria: CV API clearly distinguishes axes; LOSO/K-fold subject CV supported; reference selection is training-only; tests cover leakage guard.

description: Clarify/encode whether a fitted model can (a) apply an existing subject operator to new data for that subject, (b) produce an operator for a new subject without refitting (usually no), and (c) support out-of-sample projection for embedding methods. Reflect this in the aligner contract and capabilities.

Added returns capability ("operator", "coupling", "points"). apply_alignment.R checks supports_new_subject before fitting transforms for new subjects. fit_new parameter controls whether to fit or skip. All aligners have these capabilities set appropriately.

acceptance_criteria: A short design note in neuralign docs describing dkge adapter requirements + recommended capabilities metadata.

title: Add anchor safety + fold-spec support for CV results
description: Improve CV/crossfit safety: (1) accept explicit fold specs in fit_alignment(), (2) record CV axis + anchor provenance, (3) expose has_common_anchor()/validate_common_anchor() so downstream group stats can refuse leaky/fold-specific anchor results, and (4) warn/guard conversions like as_map_family() when CV result lacks common anchor.

title: Embedding methods: document recommended pattern (operators + optional embeddings)
description: Update docs (PRD/ARCHITECTURE/roxygen) to clarify: neuralign core is operator-based; embedding methods can still integrate by returning operators (possibly rectangular projections) and storing embeddings in method_state. Document how dkge should present its outputs.
acceptance_criteria: Docs clearly state operator convention, how to represent projections, and what 'returns=embedding' means in practice.
close_reason: Documented current operator-only stance: PRD clarifies embedding methods must expose operators and store extra artifacts in method_state; registry docs mark 'embedding' as reserved.

title: Add pseudoinverse/regularized options to inverse_transform
description: Extend neuralign::inverse_transform() beyond exact inverse: add method='pinv' (Moore-Penrose) and method='ridge' (Tikhonov-regularized), and make method='auto' strict (transpose for orthogonal/permutation; solve for general invertible; error for non-invertible/non-square/OT with guidance). Add tests + docs.
close_reason: Implemented inverse_transform(method='pinv'|'ridge') with tests/docs; fixed roxygen internal docs + warning.

title: Replace O(features²) quality computation with scalable row-wise correlation
description:
.compute_basic_quality() in fit_alignment.R:553-574 uses cor(t(x), t(y)) which creates an O(features²) matrix, only to extract the diagonal. For fMRI-scale data this is an OOM risk.

A scalable row-wise implementation already exists in quality.R:98-103 (.compute_correlation_metrics) and reference.R:288-294. The fix is to replace the cor(t(x),t(y)) pattern with row-wise centering + dot product, which is O(features × obs).

Additionally consider:
- Defaulting compute_quality=FALSE or using a feature subsample by default
- Documenting the memory implications
close_reason: Replaced cor(t(x),t(y)) quality with overlap-aware row-wise correlation (O(features×obs))

title: Introduce operator abstraction and composition rules
description: Define an operator type that can be dense/sparse matrix, callable, or descriptor (e.g., on-disk warp path). Standardize composition semantics and validation (target×source). Ensure compatibility with fmrigds MapFamily expectations.
acceptance_criteria: compose_alignment works for matrix+matrix and sparse+matrix; operator validation catches dimension/space mismatches; unit tests added.
close_reason: implemented

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Implemented: compose.R provides compose_alignment() function and "%+%" operator for composing AlignmentModel objects. Composition follows left-multiply convention: (A %+% B) means apply B first, then A. S4 compose method defined for AlignmentModel class. Matrix multiplication handles dimension compatibility.

title: Formalize and document apply_fn signature contract
description:
apply_fn is an optional slot in the aligner registry but its contract is implicit. It's called differently in different places:

- fit_alignment.R:507-514 (CV new subject): passes fit_result + new_data
- apply_alignment.R:172-186 (new data application): reconstructs fit_result from AlignmentModel slots

The reconstructed fit_result in apply_alignment.R is a plain list, not the actual fit result.

Standardize on a canonical signature:
  apply_fn(fit_result, new_data, ...) -> list(transforms=...)

Consider whether apply_fn should receive the AlignmentModel directly instead of a reconstructed fit_result list, so apply logic has consistent access to all model state.

Document the expected input/output schema in register_aligner() roxygen.
close_reason: Implemented and tested

title: Expand aligner capability metadata
description: Extend capabilities beyond needs_geometry/needs_design: cv_axes, returns (operator_family vs embedding), transform_type, invertibility, uncertainty support. Use this metadata for validation and helpful errors.
acceptance_criteria: register_aligner validates capabilities; fit/apply use metadata to gate unsupported operations; available_aligners() reports capabilities.
close_reason: implemented

comments.author: claude
comments.text: Implemented: Expanded default capabilities in registry.R to include: cv_axes (list of CV axes), supports_new_subject, supports_new_data, returns ("operator"/"coupling"/"points"). All aligners (procrustes, GW, FPGW) updated with expanded capabilities. OT methods correctly specify returns="coupling".

title: Define contract for embedding-returning aligners
description: Current neuralign assumes all methods return left-multiply operators. dkge (and similar) may naturally return embeddings/projections. Define and implement a supported pathway: either (a) require aligners with returns='embedding' to provide apply_fn that yields operators, or (b) extend AlignmentModel/apply_alignment/compose_alignment to support embedding/projector semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Registering an aligner with capabilities='embedding' produces either a working apply path or a clear, early error with guidance. Document expected fit_fn/apply_fn behavior for embedding methods.
close_reason: Decided operator-only core: register_aligner rejects returns='embedding' with guidance; added operator validation in fit_alignment/apply_alignment/compose_alignment; updated docs and tests.

title: Decide dependency strategy for canonical wrappers
description: Resolve whether neuralign ships canonical wrappers for Procrustes/OT (requiring Imports on manifoldalign) versus splitting wrappers into plugin packages. Update DESCRIPTION accordingly and document the plugin registration story to avoid cycles.
acceptance_criteria: Documented policy; DESCRIPTION Imports/Suggests consistent; at least one canonical method works out of the box.
close_reason: completed

title: Add model-only workflow to fit_alignment()
description:
fit_alignment() always materializes aligned data matrices in AlignmentResult@aligned. For N subjects with dims (n_feat × n_obs), this is N × n_feat × n_obs × 8 bytes of memory that's often unnecessary in pipelines.

Add one of:
- return_aligned=TRUE/FALSE parameter
- fit_alignment(..., apply=FALSE)
- fit_alignment_model() that returns only AlignmentModel

Same consideration for apply_alignment() (sometimes you only want new transforms added, not the aligned data).

This matters for ecosystem delegation where downstream packages call fit_alignment() as infrastructure.
close_reason: Implemented and tested

title: Feature block helpers: stack + harmonize
description: Add lightweight feature-block constructors, stacking (sqrt-weighted rbind), and cross-subject harmonization by intersecting feature names.
close_reason: Added feature block constructor, stacking, and cross-subject harmonization helpers

title: Core clarity: profiles + feature-block metadata
description:
Make neuralign's public surface crystal clear and modular by explicitly separating domain-agnostic primitives from optional domain 'profiles'.

Scope:
- Add optional metadata support for feature blocks so downstream packages can tag blocks (e.g., source_type, requires_independence) without neuralign hardcoding fMRI semantics.
- Refactor docs so vignettes clearly distinguish 'core' vs 'fMRI profile/recipes' and avoid package-specific framing in core docs.

Non-goals:
- No fmrireg/NEF/graphlowrank objects or heuristics in neuralign core; client packages remain responsible for feature extraction and fold policy.

title: Feature blocks: optional meta/tags
description:
Extend alignment_feature_block() to accept an optional "meta" list (opaque to neuralign) and preserve it through harmonize_feature_blocks().

Design constraints:
- Remains fully domain-agnostic; neuralign does not interpret meta keys.
- Backward compatible: meta defaults to NULL/list(); existing callers unchanged.
- Validation: meta must be NULL or a list.

Acceptance:
- Tests cover: constructor validation, meta preservation through harmonization (including feature subsetting/reordering).
- Docs describe suggested generic keys (e.g., source_type, requires_independence) as recommendations only.

title: Docs: split core vs fMRI profile recipes
description:
Refactor documentation so neuralign core stays general and profile-specific conventions are clearly labeled as optional recipes.

Changes:
- Update vignettes so core docs avoid package-specific framing (no graphlowrank/gnef names in core narrative).
- Move fMRI-specific block vocabulary/weighting/crossfit guidance into a dedicated 'fMRI profile' vignette or docs page (examples only; no hardcoded semantics).
- Keep anchors vignette focused on the general regimes (shared labels, sparse overlap, guidance channels) with pointers to profiles.

Acceptance:
- Vignettes render under R CMD check.
- Clear statement of the core/profile boundary and non-goals.

title: Allow variable feature dims for methods that support it
description: Refactor fit_alignment()/validate_alignment_data usage so aligners can declare whether they require shared feature dims and/or observation dims. Needed for anatomy-guided and OT-based methods where subjects may have different voxel/vertex counts.
close_reason: Made fit_alignment dimension validation method-aware via capabilities requires_shared_features/observations

title: Fix fmrigds integration to use exported API
description: R CMD check WARNING: neuralign references missing/unexported fmrigds symbols (gds_subjects, gds_get_data, gds_apply_maps, gds_space) and uses an outdated MapFamily constructor signature. Update R/compat_fmrigds.R to use exported fmrigds generics (subjects(), space(), assay(), align()/align_eager, MapFamily(name, from_space, to_space, type, by_subject, ...)). Remove or gate any calls to non-exported fmrigds functions.
acceptance_criteria: R CMD check has no 'Missing or unexported objects' warnings for fmrigds; as_map_family()/from_map_family()/apply_to_gds()/alignment_data_from_gds() work against current fmrigds API.
close_reason: Fixed compat layer to use fmrigds exported API; R CMD check no longer reports missing/unexported fmrigds symbols.

title: Add validate_aligner_contract() and API versioning for third-party aligners
description:
The aligner registration interface is implicit. Third-party packages registering aligners have no way to validate their implementation against the expected contract.

Add:
1. NEURALIGN_ALIGNER_API_VERSION constant (start at 1)
2. validate_aligner_contract(entry) function that checks:
   - Required fields in capabilities
   - fit_fn signature expectations (data, reference, train_idx, ...)
   - Output schema: transforms, reference_data, space_from, space_to, optional method_state
   - apply_fn signature if provided (fit_result, new_data, ...)
   - Return value schema for apply_fn
3. Require aligners to declare the API version they implement
4. Call validate_aligner_contract() from register_aligner()

This prevents silent drift as the aligner interface evolves and makes delegation to ecosystem packages more robust.
close_reason: Implemented and tested

title: Ecosystem: graphlowrank feature-block unification
description:
Unify graphlowrank/fmrireg.lowrank's internal feature-block alignment plumbing with neuralign::alignment_feature_block(), harmonize_feature_blocks(), and stack_feature_blocks(), while making conventions (left/right Procrustes, weight semantics) explicit.

Goal: keep domain-specific extraction (betas/contrasts/priors) in graphlowrank, but centralize representation/harmonization/stacking in neuralign.
close_reason: Completed vk5.1-3: feature-block spec + migration guide in vignette, and identifiability diagnostics helper with tests/docs.

title: Spec: block taxonomy + orientation + weight semantics
description:
Write a short spec for how graphlowrank should express its correspondence signals as neuralign feature blocks.

Include:
- Block taxonomy (suggested names like task_beta, contrast_beta, roi_fingerprint, anat_feature).
- Orientation conventions:
  - If aligning anchor basis via right-multiply (F_s %*% O_s), represent blocks as (correspondence_rows × K) and use procrustes_rotation(convention='right').
  - If using fit_alignment() (left-multiply), represent data as t(F_s) (K × correspondence) and interpret returned Q as t(O_s).
- Weight semantics:
  - neuralign stacks with sqrt(weight); graphlowrank currently uses linear multiply.
  - Decide on policy: map legacy w -> w^2 for backward compatibility or adopt sqrt-weight with deprecation.

Deliverable: markdown section in docs (or vignette), plus a clear recommendation for default semantics.
close_reason: Documented block taxonomy, Procrustes orientation conventions, and weight semantics for downstream feature-block workflows.

title: Guide: graphlowrank migration to neuralign feature_blocks
description:
Provide a migration guide for fmrireg.lowrank/graphlowrank:

- Given per-subject betas/contrasts, show how to construct alignment_feature_block() objects with feature_names set to regressor/contrast ids.
- harmonize_feature_blocks() to intersect/reorder across subjects.
- stack_feature_blocks() to build F_s.
- procrustes_rotation(..., convention='right') to recover basis rotations O_s.

Also cover sparse label overlap cases and when to switch to procrustes_graph.

Deliverable: vignette section or docs page that downstream packages can follow mechanically.
close_reason: Added a mechanical graphlowrank migration recipe (blocks -> harmonize -> stack -> procrustes_rotation) including sparse-overlap fallback via procrustes_graph.

title: Diagnostics: identifiability / effective-rank reporting for stacked blocks
description:
Add optional diagnostics helpers for feature-block alignment workflows:

- Compute per-block and stacked effective rank / singular value spectra.
- Report fraction of feature space identified by correspondence blocks.
- Provide a small summary object usable by downstream packages (graphlowrank, gnef).

This supports the story: design-driven alignment identifies only the excited subspace; adding blocks increases identifiability.

Deliverable: an exported helper (name TBD) + tests + documentation.
close_reason: Implemented feature_block_diagnostics() with per-block + stacked effective-rank reporting, plus tests and documentation.

title: Add spaces_compatible() helper for space object comparison
description:
There is no space compatibility checking infrastructure. apply_alignment() has no space mismatch warnings at all, and compose_alignment() doesn't validate space chain compatibility.

Add a spaces_compatible(a, b) generic that:
- For gds_space objects: compare name and dimensions/affine
- For character spaces: simple equality
- Fallback: isTRUE(all.equal(a, b)) or class match
- Handle NULL (compatible with anything)

Use in:
- apply_alignment() to warn when model@space_from != new_data@space
- compose_alignment() to validate model1@space_to is compatible with model2@space_from
close_reason: Implemented and tested

title: procrustes_graph: new-subject support + CV friendliness
description:
Make the procrustes_graph aligner usable as a general backend for packages with sparse/partial obs_labels overlap (e.g., missing regressors/features/time segments).

Scope:
- Add apply_fn so apply_alignment() can align a new subject to an existing procrustes_graph model using overlap labels (generic, not fMRI-specific).
- Update capabilities so subject-axis CV can work when overlap with the model reference is sufficient.

Non-goals:
- No domain heuristics for choosing overlaps; strictly label-based matching + Procrustes.

title: procrustes_graph: apply_alignment() for new subjects
description:
Implement an apply_fn for the procrustes_graph aligner so new subjects can be aligned to an existing model.

Design:
- Store reference obs_labels in method_state during fit.
- In apply_fn, compute a Procrustes rotation between new subject and the model reference using label overlap (min_overlap enforced), returning a left-multiply operator to the reference space.
- If overlap is insufficient, error with a diagnostic (suggest adding anchors or lowering min_overlap).

Acceptance:
- Tests: apply_alignment(model, new_data) succeeds when overlap >= min_overlap; fails cleanly otherwise.
- Update aligner capabilities: supports_new_subject=TRUE; supports_cv=TRUE for subject-axis CV when reference is fixed.

title: procrustes_graph: overlap-aware reference selection (optional)
description:
Investigate and (if sensible) implement support for reference specs beyond fixed subject IDs in procrustes_graph (e.g., reference="medoid" resolved to a subject id using an overlap-aware distance).

Notes:
- The standard select_reference(distance="procrustes") assumes shared observation dimensions; sparse-overlap requires label-aware distances.
- If implemented, keep it generic: distances defined on overlaps via obs_labels.

Acceptance:
- Either: implement reference="medoid" (and document anchor_common implications), or explicitly document why fixed-subject reference is required and add an early validation error path.
